text: Someresidence permitshave their own online application form: Opportunity card Student visa Blue Card Work visa for people with a university degree Work visa for people with professional training Freelance visa Citizenship Permanent residenceFor Blue Card holdersFor the family of German citizensFor skilled workersFor refugees and asylum seekersEU permanent residence(what’s the difference?) For Blue Card holders For the family of German citizens For skilled workers For refugees and asylum seekers EU permanent residence(what’s the difference?) See the full list If your residence permit is not in this list, use thecontact formto send your application.

title: Use the contact form
text: To contact theAusländerbehörde, or to apply for a residence permit that is not inthis list, you must… Find your department Use the contact formFind your department’s contact form. Write in German. If you don’t speak German, useDeepl. If it’s urgent, use theemergency form. Your message must include…Your name and date of birthWhat you needThe expiration date of your visa or residence permitIf your visa or residence permit expires soon, ask for aFiktionsbescheinigung7 Your name and date of birth What you need The expiration date of your visa or residence permit If your visa or residence permit expires soon, ask for aFiktionsbescheinigung7 Attach your documentsAdd your application documents to your message. Complete applications are processed faster.9You can only upload 5 small files. Use PDF files or photos, nothing else. If you have too many documents,merge themandmake them smaller. If you still have too many documents, mail them. Send your messageIf you get an error (Anti-Spam-Schutz), it’s because you took too long to send your message. Click the back button, and send it again. After you send the message, clickZusammenfassung ausdruckento print the confirmation message. This is a proof of your residence permit application. You might not get a confirmation email.8 Wait for a responseThey replyvery slowly. If you wait more than 3 months, you cansue theAusländerbehörde.17If your visa or resident permit expires, it’s usually extended until theAusländerbehördeprocesses your application. Sometimes, you can’t reply to their emails directly, so you must use the contact form again. What happens next?

title: Other contact options
text: You can contact theAusländerbehördebyregistered mail, but it’s not better or faster.6You can’t call or fax them.10 Address your letter to the correctdepartment, at the correct address:Friedrich-Krause-UferorKeplerstraße. How to mail a letter

title: Emergencies
text: If it’s urgent, choose theEiliger Termin/Notfallcategory in the contact form.1

title: Locations
text: In Berlin, there are 3 immigration office locations. Choose the correct one. Friedrich-Krause-Ufer Keplerstraße Fasanenstraße(Business Immigration Service)

title: Departments
text: The Berlin immigration office has multiple departments. Send your application to the correct one. B1, B2, B3, B4For skilled workers, students, researchers and their family. They handleBlue Cards,work visas,student visasand more. B6 –Business Immigration Service(BIS)For skilled workers and their family. They handleBlue Cardsandwork visas. They are usually faster than other departments. F1, F2For privileged countries. They handlepermanent residence,freelance visas, and everything else. M1, M2, M3, M4For everyone else. They handle permanent residence, freelance visas, and everything else.Choose the departmentthat is responsible for your country. S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6For citizenship applications.Choose the departmentthat is responsible for your country. List of departments Wait times by department

To visit theAusländerbehörde, you need an appointment. If you go without an appointment, they will not help you.3 You can’t book an appointment yourself.2You mustapply for a residence permitoruse their contact form. They decide when they give you an appointment. They usually takemonthsto reply.

It takes 3 to 6 months to get aresidence permitin Berlin. The wait times vary by department and residence permit type. Ausländerbehörde wait times Usually, you can’tstart workingbefore you get your residence permit. It might be cheaper to apply in your home country, and move to Berlin after you get permission to work. You don’t need to wait in Berlin without an income. How to apply in your country You don’t need a residence permit to start studying. You can start studying as soon as you arrive in Germany.18

At theAusländerbehörde, you can pay with Visa, Mastercard, cash orGirocard.4 When you apply for a residence permit online, you sometimes need to pay in advance, during your application. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash orGirocard.5

title: How to pay
text: At the end of your appointment, you get a plasticpayment card(Kassenkarte). Bring it to apayment machine(Kassenautomat). Followthe signsto find it. These machines accept cash, EC cards, Visa and Mastercard.4If your card is not accepted, get cash from an ATM. After you paid, you can go home. You don’t need to go back to your case worker. The fee istax-deductible, so keep the receipt.

TheAusländerbehördehas 3 months to process yourresidence permitapplication. If it takes longer, you can sue them.11It costs €700to €3,000.16Suing does not always work. TheAusländerbehördesometimes ignores court orders.15 First, your lawyer sends a scary letter to theAusländerbehörde. TheAusländerbehördewants to avoid a lawsuit, so they process your application faster. If the scary letter does not work, you can sue theAusländerbehörde. The legal system is slow, so a lawsuit can take months or years. If you win, theAusländerbehördemust pay for your legal fees. Usually, theAusländerbehördereacts before your case goes to court, so you must pay your own legal fees.12 In other words, you pay a few hundred euros, and thingssometimesgo faster. A lawyer can pressure theAusländerbehörde, but they can’t help you skip the queue.13 In other cities, threatening to sue theAusländerbehördecan make things worse. TheAusländerbehördecan become very strict, ask for more documents, and make your application even slower.14 Find an immigration lawyer Fiona Macdonaldis the immigration lawyer I work with. She has experience with suing theAusländerbehörde, and she speaks English.

The immigration office does not give immigration advice. Animmigration lawyeror arelocation consultantcan answer your questions. You can also get free advice from some organisations.
